title: WPSS/3491/2018 of MAMTA SAH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND, THROUGH ITS SECRETARY ELEMENTARY EDUCATION SECRETARIAT

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 3491 of 2018
Mamta Sah .......Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand & others .....Respondents
Mr. Anil Kumar Joshi, Advocate, for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, Standing Counsel, for the State of Uttarakhand.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
 The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner was
appointed with the respondent No.5, to the writ petition, as an
Assistant Teacher (General) in the Pay Scale of 9300-34800, with the
Grade Pay of Rs.4600. The petitioner contends that ever since her
initial appointment on 4th March 2013, and she continued to serve the
respondent No.5, in the said capacity till the institution was
considered, and brought under grant-in-aid with effect from 4th March
2014.
2. The petitioner contends that as per the Rules applicable,
for the purposes of determining the eligibility criteria for making a
candidate eligible to be appointed he or she, has had to have a
qualification of TET. This fact cannot be disputed because of the
enforcement of the Rules itself, the eligibility criteria of a candidate,
who was supposed to be considered was the eligibility status as it was
existing, on 13th May 2012, that is prior to the petitioner's
appointment. The said stipulations provided under the Rules, as it was
then existing on 13th May 2012, could not be applied in the present set
of circumstances, as it has been argued by the petitioner, that
subsequent to the Institution being brought into grant-in-aid on 4th
March 2014, the petitioner's contention is that she completed her
CTET on 7th November, 2016 and TET 2 on 7th March 2017,
meaning thereby she was qualified to hold the post.

2
3. These two figures of having qualified the two
examinations, which were the basic eligibility qualification which was
required for recruitment of an Assistant Teacher (General), is not a
fact which had been denied by the petitioner, because the said
qualification itself has been taken into consideration while passing the
impugned order dated 6th June, 2018, holding thereof, that the
petitioner on the date of her alleged appointment was not holding the
qualification to make her eligible to be considered for appointment.
However, the cut-off which has been considered in the impugned
order is that of 13th May 2012.
4. The argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner is
that the said cut-off, which has been extracted, to make the petitioner
ineligible to be considered for appointment in accordance with the
Right to Education Act, will not be sustainable for the reason being
that, the Legislature by virtue of an amendment made by the
amending Act No.24 of 2017, Right to Children to Free and
Compulsory Education (Amendment) Act 2017, had amended Section
2 of the Right to Education Act, and by virtue of the amendment made
under Section 2 which was brought into effect with effect from 9th
August 2017. The amended provision read as under:
"2. In the Right of Children to Free and
Compulsory Education Act, 2009, in Section 23
in sub-section (2) after the proviso, the
following proviso shall be inserted, namely:-
 Provided further that every teacher
appointed or in position as on the 31st March,
2015, who does not possess minimum
qualifications as laid down under sub-section
(1), shall acquire such minimum
qualifications within a period of four years
from the date of commencement of the Right
of Children to Free and Compulsory
Education (Amendment) Act, 2017."
5. If the proviso, which was added to Section 23 (2) of the
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, if
that is taken into consideration, an exception was carved out, and it
further provided that although Teachers, who were appointed or were
in possession of qualification prior to 31st March 2015, which happens

3
to be the case of the petitioner, she would be falling within the zone of
consideration for the reason being that it is a specific case of the
petitioner that she was appointed on 4th March, 2013, she was still
working in the Institution, at the time when the Institution was taken
in grant-in-aid in the year 2014, and hence the cut-off provided for
extending the period for acquiring the requisite qualification as
provided by the amended proviso of the amending Act No.24 of 2017,
there was an extension of time which was granted for the purpose of
procuring the qualification within a period of four years from the date
of the commencement of the amending Act. Meaning thereby, the
amendment, which was brought into effect with effect from 9th August
2017, the cut-off of four years for acquiring the eligibility
qualification prescribed under Section 23 (2) in the Act of 2009,
would be treated to have been extended till 8th August 2021. In fact, in
that eventuality if the amending Act is taken into consideration, the
petitioner's since had already acquired the TET 2 qualification on 7th
March 2017, which itself is quite apparent from the impugned order
dated 6th June 2018, the petitioner's candidature cannot be ousted on
the basis of the logic, which has been assigned in the impugned order,
that the petitioner was not having the requisite eligible qualification
when the recruitment process was held, and as was required under the
Right to Education Act on 13th May 2012. In fact, the date of 13th May
2012 becomes irrelevant for consideration for denying the claim of the
petitioner because of her own appointment having being of 4
th May
2013, because of the fact that she was working in the Institution on
31st March 2015, that is cut-off provided by the proviso added to
Section 23 by the amending Act No.24 of 2017.
6. In that eventuality, if at all the petitioner's claim was to
be considered for the grant of approval to her appointment as an
Assistant Teacher (General), it was to be taken into consideration, it
ought to have been in the light of the amended provision, provided by
amending Act No.24 of 2017. Having failed to consider the
petitioner's claim for approval of her appointment in the light of the
amended provisions itself, renders the order to be vitiated, and based

4
on the wrongful interpretation of attracting the date of 13th May 2012,
as to be a cut-off provided under the Right to Education Act.
7. In that eventuality, and owing to the apparent facts which
had been brought on record, this Court is of the considered view, that
in view of the amending Act No.24 of 2017, which extended the
period of time, within which the Teacher can acquire an eligible
qualification under Section 23 of the Act i.e. within a period of four
years, and since the petitioner had acquired TET 2 examination on 7th
March 2017, that is even much prior to the enforcement of the
amending Act, the petitioner cannot be held to be non suited to be
considered for granting of an appointment as an Assistant Teacher
(General) by the respondents.
8. In that view of the matter the impugned order dated 6th
June 2018, rejecting the petitioner's claim for being granted approval
to her appointment an Assistant Teacher (General) is hereby set aside.
The District Education Officer, Tehri Garhwal; as well as Chief
Education Officer, are directed to pass an order fresh for the purposes
of considering the petitioner's claim for grant of appointment and to
her approval as an Assistant Teacher (General) taking into
consideration the qualification of the petitioner itself having acquired
TET on 7th March 2017, as well as the impact of the proviso to the
amended Act No. 24 of 2017. A writ of mandamus is hereby issued to
the respondents to grant an approve the status of the petitioner's
appointment as an Assistant Teacher (General), in the light of the
amending Act No.24 of 2017, and it is hoped and trusted that the
respondent Nos.3 and 4, may pass an appropriate order of approving
the appointment of the petitioner based on the qualification possessed
by the petitioner within a period of one month from the date of the
production of a certified copy of this judgment.
9. Subject to the above observations, the writ petition stands
allowed
10. It is goes without saying that since the petitioner status of

5
appointment as an Assistant Teacher (General) has been upheld to be
that of the regular appointee since having the requisite qualification
with effect from 7th March 2017, the petitioner would be entitled for
the admissible pay-scale in accordance with law, for the period during
which the issue remain pending before this Court after acquiring of
her qualification of TET 2.
